title: Central Authority's Power to Prohibit Endorsers of False or Misleading Advertisements

content.scenario: A popular Indian actor endorses a new fitness program, claiming that it can help users get six-pack abs in just one month. The Central Authority investigates and finds that the claim is false and misleading.
content.outcome: The Central Authority may prohibit the actor from making endorsements for any product or service for a period of up to one year, and up to three years for subsequent contraventions, as per the provisions of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

user_queries: What can the Central Authority do to an endorser of a false advertisement?
Can the Central Authority prohibit an endorser from making future endorsements?
How does the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 regulate prohibitions on endorsers?
